name: Init order
info:
Startup

1. CONSTANTS
2. CONFIG
3. PREFS
4. HOST
5. UTILS
6. DEVICES
7. STATE
8. Validate Startup
9. Startup Complete

CONSTANTS has no dependencies.
CONFIG may use constants.
PREFS may depend on configuration (default values, storage location, etc.).
HOST is independent and can be collected early.
UTILS may use constants/config.
DEVICES will almost certainly use CONSTANTS, CONFIG, and possibly PREFS.
STATE is last because it represents the initial runtime state after everything else exists.

info:
Notification receives events, evaluates notification policy, and if 
policy dictates, generates one or more notifications using the 
appropriate transport(s).

Responsibilities
    Send email using the configured SMTP server.
    Report success or failure to the caller.
    Hide the SMTP implementation details.

Not Responsible For
    Deciding whether an email should be sent.
    Duplicate suppression.
    Rate limiting.
    Notification policy.
    Message prioritization.
    Formatting notifications.
    Choosing recipients based on event type.

Input
    msg.topic      Subject
    msg.payload    Plain text body
    msg.to         Optional recipient override

Output
    None

name: NOTIFICATION
info:
Responsibilities
    Receive notification requests from other subsystems.
    Decide whether the requested notification is currently enabled.
    Prevent duplicate notifications (eventually).
    Apply rate limiting (eventually).
    Choose one or more delivery transports.
    Format the notification message.
    Request delivery from the selected transport(s).
Not Responsible For
    Detecting failures.
    Monitoring devices.
    Sending email.
    Sending SMS.
    Logging events.
    Maintaining device state

Receive notification event
        │
        ▼
Generate notification key
        │
        ▼
Already in activeNotifications?

        Yes
            Done.

        No
            Create ACTIVE_NOTIF
            Populate it
            Add to activeNotifications
            Done.

    Monitoring system health.
    Sending notifications.
    Device registration.
